name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 7 years' residence; good character and conduct with no convictions for corruption or sex crimes and no participation in genocide, terrorism, treason, or war crimes; and either distinguished service to the nation or a showing that naturalization will benefit the state -- a genuinely restrictive standard, not a routine formality. Applications require approval by both the Council of Ministers and the National Assembly before the President grants naturalization. Successful applicants must renounce other nationalities.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 7 years' residence, maintain a clean record, and demonstrate distinguished service or state benefit, then obtain Council of Ministers and National Assembly approval ahead of a presidential grant.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of distinguished service or state benefit

sources.title: Wikipedia -- 7-year residency requirement, the Council of Ministers/National Assembly/presidential approval chain, the 'distinguished service or state benefit' restrictive standard, and the constitutional dual-citizenship ban described as tolerated in practice since 2002
Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- corroborates the constitutional dual-nationality ban and its described tolerance in practice since 2002

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Democratic Republic of the Congo). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to tier-3/4 only; the 2004 Nationality Code's own text was not locatable/fetchable in this build. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE FINDING, HEAVY DISCRETION: naturalization requires approval by BOTH a legislative body (National Assembly) AND the executive (President via Council of Ministers) -- a dual political gate not seen in this exact combined form elsewhere in this dataset, on top of an already-restrictive 'distinguished service or state benefit' standard rather than a routine residency-plus-language test. LAW-VERSUS-PRACTICE TENSION ON DUAL CITIZENSHIP, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: the constitution formally bans dual nationality, and this file's dual_citizenship_allowed is set false to reflect that formal legal position, but multiple sources describe multiple-nationality holding as having been 'tolerated in practice since 2002' -- a real gap between the law on paper and reported enforcement that this dataset's schema cannot cleanly express as a single boolean. This tension is disclosed consistently across cd_citizenship_by_descent.json and cd_citizenship_by_marriage.json's notes as well, rather than asserting different values in different files without explanation.
